community-s12b.u1b1:
This article asks people to discuss jealousy, God, death, childhood, money, sex, psychedelics, and what happens when somebody wants to leave. Many perfectly intelligent adults would rather discuss solar panels for six hours.

I understand why. Modern life trains us to perform competence while hiding whatever might complicate the performance. Screens let us disappear from discomfort instantly. Institutions reward narrow skills and then act surprised when nobody can sit through a conflict without appointing a subcommittee or blocking somebody.
community-s12b.u1b2-emuA:
To what extent do people want to talk about jealousy, God, death, their childhood, money, sex, psychedelics, or the fact that one of them wants to leave? People will talk about solar panels for six hours, but it’s much rarer to discuss these topics, and it’s not for lack of interest, it’s the people are intelligent adults.

It comes down to the structure of modern life. People want to feel they’re doing what they’re supposed to be doing, or at least doing some part of that. It’s an accident, and it’s exacerbated by all the screens and such, but it exists, and it’s because people only really know how to do one or two things. If something comes up, it’s natural to want to make a committee, appoint a sub-committee, or just hit block.
